newsitem.title: JAPAN: New NCB shares to be priced below market - paper.
newsitem.headline: New NCB shares to be priced below market - paper.

text.p: New shares in Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) to be issued as part of a rescue package for the troubled bank will be priced below the market, the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday.
No dividend will be paid on the shares for the first five years and the payout on preferred shares will be limited to one percent in order to lighten the bank's financial burden, the paper said.
NCB said it would issue a statement on reports of a capital increase at 10.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).

Under a scheme devised by Japan's Finance Ministry, the Bank of Japan will buy 80 billion yen of preferred NCB shares and private sector financial institutions will purchase 70 billion yen of common shares.
In addition, insurance companies would convert 150 billion yen in subordinated loans owed by Nippon Credit Bank into 100 billion yen of common shares and 50 billion yen of preferred shares.
A Finance Ministry spokesman was not immediately available to comment.

The bank on Tuesday announced restructuring measures aimed at restoring its financial health. It said it hoped the measures, which included halting overseas operations, would boost its capital by 300 billion yen.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that the ministry had asked the Bank of Japan and a special body administering a fund to wind up failed finance firms for permission to use the fund to buy preferred stock to be issued by NCB.
